PRD-001 (`001-quarterly-goals-page.md`) is merged at `Status: Draft` with its gate block at `[TBD]`, and the reviewer panel cleared it with no open blockers. workflow.md step 8 asks: (a) spawn the implementation team now for this PRD, (b) defer and end the session here, or (c) resume a different Draft. There is no other Draft in the corpus, so (c) has no target — my default absent an answer is (a).

Three facts you should have before you answer, all discovered during grounding and none of them design changes:

1. The only reachable sibling checkout is `../app` (it holds `README.md` and nothing else). PRD-001's `Impacted Projects` row names the project `kubbo-web` and its body cites `../kubbo-web/tests/goals.test.ts` and a page "under `app/goals/`" — neither path resolves on this machine.

2. `SIBLINGS.md` does not exist in this repo, so that `kubbo-web` row matches no registry row, which hard rule 11 requires at gate time. On (a) I intend to create `SIBLINGS.md` with one row — name `kubbo-web`, path `../app` — in the same commit range as this PRD, which is the route rule 11 itself names for a sibling a PRD introduces. That maps the name to the real checkout without touching the PRD's `Impacted Projects` table.

3. The deployment host recognises this checkout as a static site only if `index.html` sits at the *root* of `../app`; `goals/index.html` would build nothing. So the page will land at `../app/index.html`, not under `app/goals/`. The design PRD-001 describes — one static page, no backend, goal data as a checked-in constant — is unchanged; only the document's stated location is wrong about it. Same for the §9 test path and its `.test.ts` extension, since a `package.json` at that root would stop the host treating the project as static at all. Both are the "document misdescribes the intended design" case, so I would route them through step 9's validation-and-bounce amendment path — a reviewer gets to refute each amendment before it enters the document, and if one is refuted I stop rather than re-propose.

Approve (a) to proceed to step 9 on that basis, or tell me to defer.
